Player profile

Rating, record, results at every event and who they have played. Uses the period and settings from the Rankings tab, so the numbers always match the ranking.

Head to head

Every counted set between two players, newest first.

Bracket

Pick an event to see its sets round by round. Tap a player's name (or type one) to light up their path through it; everything else fades.

Tussly

Reads every NASB2 event of the year from Tussly's public pages (no login) and adds the ones you don't have yet. Excluded series are skipped automatically. If it stops part-way (or you closed the page), press it again: events already downloaded are skipped, so it carries on where it left off.
Keep this page open and your screen on while it updates (the first full download takes a few minutes). Your data is kept in this browser only: use Backup below to save a copy.

Character & stage data (optional)

Tussly records which character each player used and which stage each game was played on; start.gg can record characters (no stages) when the organiser reports them. This fetches both for every counted set of the events you already have. Tussly takes one request per set, so the first time takes a while (roughly a second per set: a whole year can take an hour or more; keep the page open and the screen on). start.gg takes one request per page of sets, which is much quicker, and needs the token in the start.gg box below. The rankings never use any of it; it only feeds the Characters tab and a game-by-game recap on the Bracket tab. If it stops part-way, press it again: it carries on. Run Update from Tussly and Update from start.gg first.

start.gg

Your start.gg token is needed (start.gg → Profile → Developer Settings). It is kept on this device only (in settings.json on a PC, in this browser on a phone) and is never put in a backup. The app can find your year's NASB2 events by itself, and you can also paste links for events it misses, one per line.
Run Find events (preview) first: it lists every event it found and why any are skipped (team events, too few entrants, excluded series, already downloaded) without adding anything. The start.gg part has not been tried on live data yet.

Backup

Save your data (events, sets, name merges, saved rankings) as one file, or load one made on another device. Restoring replaces the data on this device, except saved rankings: those in the backup are added to the ones already here and none are removed.
Download backup

Add events from a file

Adds the events in an NASB2 events file (a .json file) with their sets and placements, for example the Challonge brackets in challonge-brackets.json. An event that is already here is replaced by the one in the file; nothing else changes, so it is safe to add the same file twice.

Publish a read-only copy

Makes one web page with your data and every saved year inside it, for anyone to open. They can use every tab, filter and sort, but cannot add or change anything, and the ranking settings are fixed to what the Rankings tab shows now. Upload the file to a web host (for example GitHub Pages, where naming it index.html gives the shortest link). Your private page stays as it is: update it, then make a new copy and upload that over the old one.
Leave out or limit events (excluded series, hosts, qualifier-only, offline and Circuit Boost events)
One entry per line, not case sensitive. Events already downloaded stay in your data; they just stop counting (greyed out below). Press Save to apply it to every ranking and view.

Events you have

Every downloaded event with how many counted sets and players it has. If an event looks too small, open it on Tussly with the link, or press Re-download. Events with a red differs are also listed under Data checks.
Prestige: sort and filter by who played
A strong event is one with a big field, or one full of top players. Top players are counted from the ranking on the Rankings tab (its period and settings), so they match what you see there.

Add or re-download one event

Paste the event's Tussly link (like https://tournament.tussly.com/some-event). It has to be one of the NASB2 events Tussly lists for the year, and excluded series and hosts (like AwesomeGamer400) are still skipped.

Check player names

The same player can appear under different spellings. Names that look like another player come first. Type the main spelling and press Save, or press Keep separate if it really is a different player. Names you ignore still count under the spelling they came with.

Events that don't add up

After each Tussly download, the sets are compared with Tussly's own leaderboard (wins and game totals). Events listed here differ, so look at them on Tussly before trusting their effect on the ranking.
